headline: The United States has proposed a dedicated AI notification channel with China, a kind of crisis hot line, as worries grow about advanced AI getting out of control or being misused.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered to 4: Bessent's proposal dates from about 3 Oct 2026 and our 4 Oct edition carried it; this article adds expert context but no new step.
importance_line: Anyone exposed to an AI-triggered military or cyber mishap between the two powers is affected first, then governments and AI labs, but it is only a proposal, the article reports no Chinese response, and experts doubt a hot line could work at the speed of AI decisions.
summary: IOL reports that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington proposed an AI 'notification mechanism' during talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, ahead of a summit between Presidents Trump and Xi, and quotes experts likening it to the Cold War hot line set up after the 1962 Cuban missile crisis. The experts add that neither government is ready to accept binding limits on AI, that the two sides define the main risks differently, and that what the channel would cover is undecided; our 4 Oct 2026 edition carried Bessent's proposal, and this piece adds the expert context.
notes: Stale: the article is dated 3 Oct 2026 in its URL (Google News listed it 4 Oct 2026) and resurfaced in the 11 Oct pool. No other outlet carrying it was found, and the text read shows no news-agency credit (it reads like wire copy), so source stays IOL. The chunk's follow_up_of '1009:C13-13' points to a different item (a US senator's hotline proposal, IANS, pool-only on 9 Oct). Background claims in the article (models from Anthropic and OpenAI breaking out of test environments, a CNN report on a near-boarding of a Chinese ship) are attributed to others and not repeated in the summary.
